Triage: lands in a new gate over `.changeset/*.md` ⇒ **`domain:devx`**; **type `Task`, `priority:p2`, `pm:queue`.**

## ⭐ Grading the mechanism card, not a fourth instance — and that framing is the card's main contribution

The filer says it plainly: 「Three instances of one mechanism have now been filed and worked one at a time. The mechanism itself has never been carded, and that is what this is.」 ⇒ Three instances is where a pattern stops being a coincidence, and carding the mechanism instead of the fourth instance is the right move at exactly the right time.

**The reading that makes it p2 rather than p3:** a `.changeset/*.md` body publishes **verbatim into the CHANGELOG at the next release**. ⇒ It is customer-facing text, and between authoring and release it is prose that ⛔ no gate evaluates for truth and ⛔ nothing re-reads when a later merge falsifies it. Three measured instances have already reached that state.

⭐ And the sharpest part, which a dispatch must not lose: **the one gate that reads a foreign changeset exists to discourage correcting it.** ⇒ The mechanism does not merely lack a check; the surrounding tooling actively pushes against the repair. Any fix has to reckon with that, not route around it.

## Fences

⛔ **Do not weaken the discouragement gate to make room for a fix.** It exists for a reason (a changeset belongs to its author's PR); if a correction path is needed, it should be an explicit one, ⛔ not a hole in that gate. Weakening a gate is a maintainer floor.
⛔ **Do not attempt to judge prose truth automatically.** The four gates the card enumerates judge *presence*, *bump level* and *classification* — mechanical properties. "Is this sentence true?" is not one, and a gate that pretends otherwise will be turned off within a month.
⚠️ The realistic shapes are narrower — re-reading pending changesets when a later merge touches what they describe, or surfacing them at release for a human read. ⛔ Neither is prescribed here; the lane decides.

⚠️ If the chosen shape needs a **new runtime third-party dependency**, that is a floor: stop and report.

## ⭐ The scale, which the card does not state and which PRICES the two candidate shapes

Measured on `origin/main` = `58a4fada7`:

| reading | value |
|:--|--:|
| pending `.changeset/*.md` in the tree | **1,382** |
| of those, declaring a **bump** (⇒ prose that will publish verbatim) | **955** |
| of those, **empty-frontmatter** no-release declarations | **427** |
| gates reading `.changeset/` | **4**, exactly as the card says |

⇒ triage's two named shapes are ⛔ **not** comparably priced. 「Surface them at release for a human read」 means putting **955** bodies in front of a person; 「re-read pending changesets when a later merge touches what they describe」 is a filter over the same 955 that only fires on the few a given diff touches. ⭐ Whatever is chosen must be argued **against this number**, ⛔ not against a dozen.

## ⭐ The repair path EXISTS and has been used exactly once — ⛔ verify before relying on it

The card says 「every correction so far has required a human-filed card, and the false text sat in the tree until one was worked」. Read on `main`: **`35c6a3453`** — *「docs(changeset): correct two present-tense claims a later PR falsified」* (PR objectui#8994) — is a commit that **did** edit a pending changeset body in place, and it is the objectui#8617 instance.

⇒ ⭐ the repair is **possible and precedented**, and it took a dedicated docs PR. ⚠️ The other two instances' changesets are still in the tree; ⛔ this seat did **not** verify whether their bodies were corrected — that is a reading for you, ⛔ not an assumption for either of us.

## ⚠️ The discouragement gate is REPORT-ONLY today

`check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` ships **report-only** by default (`OS_CHANGESET_OVERWRITE_ENFORCE=1` flips it), and its own header records that triage ruled 「report-only first if the population has legitimate modify cases」.

⇒ ⭐ the gate the card calls 「the mechanism discouraging the fix」 is a **reporter**, ⛔ not a blocker, today. That does ⛔ **not** license weakening it — triage fenced that explicitly — but it does mean the correction path is **not** mechanically barred, and any design that claims it is would be arguing from a false premise.

The new check is registered as **not** one — `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` **26 → 26**, `NOT_A_GATE` **10 → 11**. ⇒ two-sided: the check is **known** to the merge gate *and* deliberately **outside** the merge decision, and the classification says so in its own words — 「classifying it here rather than requiring it is what keeps a report-only check out of the merge decision」.

That is the correct pair, and it is the distinction a report-only gate usually gets wrong.
